title: 70 bots on my paper desk and the grader will only call one of them LIVE
author: QuanTradin
selftext:
I have 70 bots running on a paper desk right now. My own grader will only call one of them LIVE.

The split, off the screen this morning: 1 LIVE, 1 SHADOW, 1 SHELF, 67 carrying no grade at all. Not because the grader is broken, but because a grade has to be earned on a sample and most of them have not traded enough to earn one. A lot of them show "n=0 thin" next to the verdict, which is the engine saying out loud that it does not have enough trades to have an opinion.

The part I keep coming back to is the tail. The top of the list looks great. It always does, because the top of any sorted list looks great. Scroll and you get to the ones up two dollars, then a long run of zeros. That tail is the honest answer to "does this idea work", and almost every tool I have used is built to keep you from seeing it.

Everything is paper. Simulated fills at real quotes, no real money anywhere in it.

The thing I would genuinely like an argument about: is a grader that refuses to endorse 67 of your 70 ideas useful, or just demoralising. I lean useful, but I built it, so I am the wrong person to ask.
